function: system: wireless federated learning with digital and analog (AirComp) uplink over one scalar Rayleigh channel per device and the server, no antenna array and no RIS (pp. 4-5).
notes: Reason system: the link is single-antenna with no RIS, in a work that would be area 7. p. 1: "two communication schemes, i.e., digital and analog ones" are compared for federated learning, and device sampling is optimized (p. 9). p. 4: "be the channel between the k-th device and the PS" is one scalar coefficient with "Assume that the channels are independent Rayleigh fadings"; p. 5: "βk is the pre-processing factor at device k" is scalar (eq. 14). No antenna array or RIS in the system model; RIS and multi-antenna appear only in related work (p. 1: "reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) were used in [22]"; p. 2: "Considering multi-antenna scenarios"). Earlier codes not applied: no_learning, because in federated learning over the air the model trained across devices is the learned element; function, because the analog scheme is over-the-air aggregation (area 7). For the reviewer: if the work is read as a digital-versus-analog analysis and not an aggregation design, function or no_learning would come before system; the exclusion holds either way. Paper title matches the DOI (Yao et al., digital versus analog wireless federated learning).
